relevance_note: The study measured type I IFN signatures in nine patients diagnosed with A20 haploinsufficiency and prints their per-patient TNFAIP3 genotypes in Table S2 ("c.986+1 G>T, p.Lys329Asn*1 hetero").
method_note: In scope are only the nine patients diagnosed with HA20 ("Since nine patients (from six unrelated families) in the study were diagnosed with HA20") plus the three relatives named in the Table S2 footnote ("Patients 6 and 7 are the mother and grandmother of patient 5, respectively."): P6 and P7 are themselves HA20 patients, and the mother is also P6, so no extra relative rows were added. The other disease groups (AGS, SAVI, COPA, PRAAS, SLE, IPH, CAEBV, HMB, controls, the 37 undiagnosed patients, the patients of Table 2) have no TNFAIP3 variant and get no rows; their numbers are in publications.cohort_size_as_stated (94). Labels: the Table S2 patients are printed as bare numbers 1-9, so rule 1 ("the paper's own label") was not available; the text's labels P1-P19 belong to Table 2 (other patients), so the Table S2 numbering column was treated as a column of bare numbers and labels follow 'Table <n> #<value>' (D-22 addition) -> 'Table S2 #1' ... 'Table S2 #9'. No script was used: Table S2 (a text-converted supplementary table, not a Markdown pipe table) was read and transcribed by hand, and every span was checked against the file with grep. Table S2 cells are wrapped over two printed lines (e.g. 'c.986+1 G>T,' on one line, 'p.Lys329Asn*1 hetero' on the next); such values are recorded as a list of contiguous verbatim fragments, never joined. 'Age at IS analysis' was recorded as age_at_last_evaluation (the study's evaluation); no age at diagnosis is printed. Sex is not printed for patients 5, 6 and 7 (cells empty), so sex = not reported for them even though the footnote calls 6 and 7 the mother and grandmother of patient 5; vital status is not reported for any of the nine. The two TNFAIP3 variants that the paper says were newly confirmed pathogenic ('two variants (p.Lys329Asn*1 and p.Gly583*) newly confirmed to be pathogenic using a NF-kappaB reporter gene activity assay') are exactly the two variants of patients 1 and 3, so pathogenicity/functional evidence is recorded for those two variants only; for the other seven variants the paper gives no classification and none of the nine rows carries a cohort-wide statement. Variant classes (missense/nonsense/frameshift/splice) are never stated by the authors for any TNFAIP3 variant, so variant_type_as_stated = 'not reported' for all nine; zygosity 'heterozygous' is taken from the printed 'hetero' in each patient's own row. Inheritance and parental testing are not reported for any of the nine. Checklist: the paper reports almost no clinical detail for the HA20 patients (the symptoms column of Table S2 is 'None' for all nine and CRP is 'N/D' for four), so nearly all checklist items are 'not reported'; 'Crohn's disease'/'intestinal Behcet's disease' were accepted as evidence of gastrointestinal inflammation, 'lymphadenitis' as lymphoproliferation/lymphadenopathy, and 'recurrent stomatitis'/'Stomatitis' as oral ulcers, while 'abdominal pain' and 'arthralgia' were kept as separate features. No contradiction inside the paper affects an HA20 patient; note only that the abstract writes 'idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis' while the results and Table S3 write 'idiopathic pulmonary hemorrhage' (patients outside the scope of this extraction). The six families are not labelled in the paper, so family_label_in_paper = 'not reported'; the only stated family link among the nine is the footnote for patients 6 and 7.
